title: DkimConfig.public_key_b64 required at config time but not at runtime — asymmetric trust
description: DkimConfig requires both key_seed_b64 and public_key_b64 to be set. The public key is only used to call Ed25519Key::from_seed_and_public_key() — it is not pinned, published anywhere in the code, or compared against a DNS record. If the operator provides a mismatched public key (correct 32 bytes, wrong key), from_seed_and_public_key either silently accepts it or errors — behavior depends on the mail_auth library. If it silently accepts it, signatures will be cryptographically valid but verifiable only against the wrong public key. Operators reading the config docs may reasonably ask why they need to provide the public key at all when signing only needs the private seed. Consider whether public_key_b64 is actually needed by mail_auth or whether it can be derived from the seed — Ed25519 public keys are deterministically derived from the seed.
